newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe budgets for dam to boost sugar output.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe budgets for dam to boost sugar output.

text.p: Zimbabwe Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa announced Thursday a Z$343 million (US$29.8 million) allocation toward the construction of dams, including a huge dam meant to boost sugar production in the southern African state.

In his 1997/98 budget, Murerwa said the government had set aside money for Tokwe-Murkosi dam, which the government plans to build in Zimbabwe's southeastern province of Masvingo in a 40-60 percent partnership with local private companies Hippo Valley and Triangle Ltd.
He did not, however, say whether the government had paid its full 40 percent share of the cost of the dam which is expected to cost Z$390 million (US$34 million).
The two companies produce nearly all of Zimbabwe's annual average of 600,000 tonnes of sugar from Masvingo's lowveld.
Construction of the Tokwe-Murkosi was scheduled to start in April but the government's lack of money delayed the project.
Industry officials say the dam will help Zimbabwe boost its sugar output to close to two million tonnes a year when it is finished in the new century.
If construction had started in time, the dam would have been finished by 1999.
